title: Task row actions menu
prompt: Add row actions to tasks. Each row in `TaskList` needs a "⋯" menu with Rename, Duplicate, and Delete. Delete asks for confirmation before calling `useDeleteTaskMutation`, and only people allowed by `canDeleteTask` may delete. Rename can use `window.prompt` for the new title for now. The same actions also go into `TaskDetailHeader`, at a larger size. Build it as a reusable component and wire it into both places.

criteria.text: Generic, reusable menu family lives outside the feature (e.g. src/components/ui/action-menu.tsx) even though DropdownMenu already exists, and never imports feature modules, queries, mutations, task types, or policy. Task-specific parts (task record root, rename/duplicate/delete actions with their mutations and the canDeleteTask decision) live in the tasks feature and compose it. Skipping the generic family because a primitive "already covers the role" is a fail. Full credit needs both the family/feature split and no feature imports in the family.

The delete confirmation dialog is rendered outside the transient dropdown content (a persistent sibling controlled by root/adapter state), so closing the menu does not unmount it. Rendering AlertDialog inside DropdownMenuContent/DropdownMenuItem is a fail. When delete is not allowed, the dialog is not mounted either (capability composed explicitly, not auto-mounted).

Each call site composes the menu as child parts (trigger, content, the actions it wants, the delete dialog) with copy as children, so TaskList and TaskDetailHeader can omit, reorder, or relabel actions. A closed component configured from its root (e.g. `<TaskActionMenu task size onActionError />` that renders its trigger, items, copy, and dialog inside) or boolean switch props such as showDelete/canDelete/hideRename that select children are fails. The task record root may take the task once (and a shared error sink); nothing visual, no copy, no aria.

Each public part accepts the props of the primitive it renders (trigger, content, items forward primitive props and className; labels are children). No root-level prop bags such as triggerProps/contentProps/itemProps, and no displayed copy passed through root props/context.

Pending/disabled state belongs to the action that runs it (e.g. delete confirm disabled while deleting; duplicate shows its own pending) rather than one family-wide loading flag that disables everything.

The larger size is a typed `cva` on the menu content part (e.g. `ActionMenuContent size="lg"`) mirrored as a data attribute with a named group, and items read it through `group-data-[size=lg]/<name>:` selectors; the trigger, which sits outside the content, uses its primitive's own variant (Button `icon-lg`). No React context or store carries the size, no root-level size prop, no per-item className patches at the call site. Omitting size renders like the base primitives.

Delete runs through the existing mutation hook without touching query keys/QueryClient in components; the dialog stays open while pending (e.g. preventDefault on AlertDialogAction + mutateAsync/then close, or mutation callbacks that survive unmount) and closes on success; failure leaves a recoverable state.

Wrapped primitives keep their contract: props are spread, consumer className merged last via cn, consumer event handlers composed rather than replaced, required bindings (controlled open, generated ids) applied after the spread. Trigger keeps an accessible name.
Each menu instance has isolated state (one per row): no module-global store or shared singleton state that would couple rows.

Repository conventions: boolean-only optional JSX uses `&&` (no `cond ? <X/> : null`); no routine useMemo/useCallback/React.memo since React Compiler is enabled; no context or store for visual-only values; no exported types or hooks nobody uses; no `radix-ui/internal` imports.

Both TaskList rows and TaskDetailHeader use the new actions (detail header at the larger size), viewer permissions respected in both, and the project typechecks (see checks in CHANGES.patch context / no obvious type errors).
